questions.q: A student's basal metabolic rate is measured after an overnight fast, a full night's sleep and a period of quiet rest in a thermoneutral room. Which factor would be expected to increase BMR over the longer term?
options: Advanced age with loss of muscle mass
questions.explain: Thyroid hormones increase cellular metabolic activity and are important determinants of basal metabolic rate. BMR is also influenced by lean body mass, age, sex, body size and nutritional state; caloric restriction and loss of lean mass tend to lower it.

questions.q: During indirect calorimetry, a resting subject has a respiratory quotient close to 0.70. Which fuel is being oxidised predominantly?
options: A mixture with equal energy contribution from carbohydrate and fat
questions.explain: The respiratory quotient (CO2 produced divided by O2 consumed) is approximately 0.7 for predominant fat oxidation and approximately 1.0 for carbohydrate oxidation. Mixed diets produce intermediate values; protein oxidation has a value around 0.8.
